title: Implement frontend UI platform shutdown control and user notification system
description: Add a protected administrative shutdown control in the UI with multi-factor or double-confirmation modal. Display a graceful maintenance/shutdown banner and countdown timer to connected users, disable new transactional submissions, and trigger the backend graceful shutdown workflow while rendering real-time drain and shutdown status.
close_reason: Implemented frontend UI platform shutdown control with: double-confirmation modal, global shutdown banner with countdown timer, transactional form disabling, backend shutdown trigger via /admin/shutdown, real-time status polling via /actuator/shutdown-status, accessibility support, and responsive design. All tests pass.

title: Implement graceful backend shutdown and traffic draining across microservices
description: Configure Spring Boot graceful shutdown (server.shutdown=graceful, spring.lifecycle.timeout-per-shutdown-phase) across all platform services and gateway. Enable and secure the Spring Boot Actuator /actuator/shutdown endpoint. Implement lifecycle hooks to drain active in-flight requests, flush message buffers, release database connection pools gracefully, and deregister from service discovery / gateway before process exit.
notes:
Implemented graceful shutdown + traffic draining.

New package com.spring.api.hub.lifecycle:
- GracefulShutdownCoordinator: on ContextClosedEvent, flips ReadinessState.REFUSING_TRAFFIC (drives /actuator/health/readiness to OUT_OF_SERVICE), then refuses new business requests, deregisters, ends streaming feeds/buffers, then waits for in-flight work.
- InFlightRequestTracker: counts in-flight requests, awaitQuiescence(timeout).
- DrainGateWebFilter: 503 + Retry-After while draining; management endpoints exempt in both directions (a shutdown request must not wait on itself).
- ShutdownTokenWebFilter: guards /actuator/shutdown, constant-time compare. Fails closed: no token provisioned -> 404; wrong token -> 401.
- DrainSignal + MessageBufferRegistry: end the never-ending SSE feeds and hotSink.
- ServiceDeregistration SPI + LoggingServiceDeregistration default; a discovery client just publishes another bean.

Config: server.shutdown=graceful, timeout-per-shutdown-phase=30s, actuator exposure health/info/shutdown, health probes enabled, show-details=never, platform.shutdown.drain-timeout=20s, shutdown-token from HUB_SHUTDOWN_TOKEN (blank = endpoint disabled).

Key fix: the Jenkins SSE feeds polled forever, so every shutdown would have stalled for the full drain timeout. They now use takeUntilOther(drainSignal.drain()).

Incidental fix: adding actuator made RequestMappingHandlerMapping ambiguous (gateway + actuator each contribute one). NavigationService now injects by bean name, and actuator paths are excluded from the site navigation.

Verified: 98 tests, 1 failure (HubApplicationTests.contextLoads, pre-existing: committed application.properties has literal <username>/<password> placeholders and no MySQL). Confirmed it passes with a real DB via SPRING_APPLICATION_JSON. Also verified against a running jar: SIGTERM during an open SSE stream ends it cleanly and shuts down in order. Docs in hub/SHUTDOWN.md.

close_reason: Sanitized tableName across create, query, and drop actions in AdminController using AdminService validation and added unit tests
